### `exit`

*object* · **required**

What ENDING this pipeline means. THREE SHAPES, deliberately different, because confusing 'a tool said yes' with 'a person said yes' is the defect this whole block exists to prevent. `register` names the bundle-relative path of a data-quality register every one of whose issues must carry a terminal disposition — the DATA pipeline's exit since 2026-09-18, and the shape a new bundle declares. `approval` names the bundle-relative path of a separate human sign-off; it was the data pipeline's exit before that date and is kept because a bundle that already declares one must keep working. `gate`+`must_exit` names a machine verdict, for a pipeline whose completion a checker can decide. WHY `register` REPLACED `approval` AS THE SHAPE TO DECLARE: the separate file duplicated the register in a LESS informative form — one date and one name against N individually-argued dispositions — and the operator it was built for refused to sign it, having already ruled on every issue one at a time. WHAT THE COLLAPSE COSTS, stated rather than glossed: the sign-off path is one the ontology guard denies UNCONDITIONALLY, so an agent cannot write it; a register is agent-writable, so this exit rests on ATTRIBUTION (`ruled_by`, `reason`, git blame) and not on PREVENTION. Carried in mac_vocabulary.yaml#data_plane_gate.approval_missing and in the gate's own refusal text.
